approved: Universities Accord (National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Gender-based Violence) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that creates a new regulatory framework to reduce gender-based violence in higher education and hold providers accountable.
The bill would let the minister make a National Code setting standards for safety, prevention, response and governance, enforced by a new specialist unit in the Department of Education.
The Secretary could publicly disclose a provider's compliance record and share information with other regulators.
Establishes a standalone regulatory framework for preventing and responding to gender-based violence in higher education.
Gives the minister power to create a National Code as a legislative instrument.
Creates a specialist gender-based violence unit within the Department of Education.
Gives the Secretary monitoring, investigation and enforcement powers including compliance notices and civil penalties.
Allows the Secretary to disclose compliance information publicly.
Requires annual reporting on the unit's operations to Parliament.
Higher education providers, their staff and students, and the Department of Education.

The majority voted against an amendment to the usual second reading motion, which is "*that the bill be read a second time*" (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). This amendment was introduced by Tasmanian Senator [Jonathon Duniam](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/jonathon_duniam) (Liberal). ### Amendment text > *At the end of the motion, add ", but the Senate urges the Government to establish an additional National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Anti-Semitism, which:* > > *(a) makes it clear to all higher education students, staff and providers that everyone on a higher education campus has a right to be safe;* > > *(b) imposes on universities a range of obligations concerning student and staff safety which is very important given the alarming increase in anti-Semitic incidents on university campuses since 7 October 2023; and* > > *(c) ensures that higher education providers must comply with recommendations of the National Student Ombudsman concerning the National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Anti-Semitism".*

The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2025-08-25.124.2) to the usual second reading amendment, which is "*that the bill be read a second time*" (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). The amendment was introduced by Berowra MP [Julian Leeser](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/berowra/julian_leeser) (Liberal). ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House urges the Government to establish an additional National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Antisemitism, which:* > >> *(1) makes it clear to all higher education students, staff and providers that everyone on a higher education campus has a right to be safe;* >> >> *(2) imposes on universities a range of obligations concerning student and staff safety which is very important given the alarming increase in antisemitic incidents on university campuses since 7 October 2023; and* >> >> *(3) ensures that higher education providers must comply with recommendations of the National Student Ombudsman concerning the National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Antisemitism".*
Moved to exempt four listed bills from specified standing order requirements so they could be considered during the sitting period; the question was agreed to.

Supported bills establishing a national higher education code to prevent and respond to gender-based violence, citing reported sexual assault, harassment and inadequate reporting support; raised concerns about assigning regulation to the Department of Education and moved support for an additional code addressing antisemitism on university campuses.

Debated the Universities Accord (National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Gender-based Violence) Bill 2025, with concerns raised about delegated powers, regulatory bureaucracy and antisemitism on campus, while support was expressed for national safety standards, accountability and protections against gender-based violence.
